chapter: Zulu, Nice and the Punch Miller incident
title: The Punch Miller incident at the Royal Orleans party
summary: Punch Miller was turned away from the party, and Rose reached Armstrong by phone, with Georgia fainting at the call.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Getting back to Louie, there's, did you, I don't know if you told me this, when Louie came down, once he, he has Face on Time Magazine. Yeah. And, I don't know where this rumor came from, I heard, that he tried to hit a room at the Roosevelt Hotel at that time?
I don't know about that. Okay. I know when the incident came up about the, with the jazz club and all that.

With Punch Miller, you know, the story that's in the, I Remember Jazz. Uh-huh. He was staying in the Roosevelt then. Yeah. But, uh, what happened there was that I called, no, what happened then was that Punch Miller had gone out with a lot of other people to the airport to meet Louie, Louie's plane.

And, uh, Louie got off the plane and he saw Punch in the crowd. So, he told Lucille, he said, I gotta go in with the first limousine, but you stay here and you make sure that Punch comes to the party tonight at the Royal Orleans where they were having it. Uh-huh. And so she stayed behind and Louie went on. Now, I, I didn't go out to meet him and as a matter of fact, I didn't plan to go to the concert either because I didn't want to get into all that action. I didn't care much for hearing Louie in concert. Uh-huh. Anyhow, he, uh, Lucille stayed and she invited Punch and Punch was walking on air. So, that night, Punch went to the party with Alan Jaffe, who took him over there, got all dressed up and they wouldn't let him in.
Well, they wouldn't let him in. Uh, nobody said why, but obviously it was because he was black. So, uh, so he was very much upset by that.

So Jaffe calls me on the phone, tells me what happened and he says, I'm sure that Louie doesn't know anything about that and you can probably get to him. I said, okay. So I called the hotel, I called the Roosevelt, talked with Ira, told him the situation. And I said, tell him to give me a ring when he gets back. So Ira said, I'm sure he will. Well, I had to go out for a few minutes. And I did. I had a maid named Georgia who was taking care of Rex when he was little. And, uh, so he called while I was gone. Georgia answered the phone and he said, this is Louis Armstrong and she fainted. So I didn't know anything about it. See, I came back and I found the phone hanging there and Georgia was going about her business in the kitchen. I said, why is the phone off the hook, Georgia? She says, I don't know. So I hung it back up and just then the phone rang right away again and it was Louis. He said, some lady answered the phone and then she didn't talk no more. So anyway, uh, he said, look, he said, I'm really, I'm sorry this happened, but if you could get, uh, punch over for the concert, see, have him come backstage. And, uh, he said, I'll take care of him. So I called Jaffe and I told him to bring punch around and Jaffe said, I don't know if I can get him to go now. So I said, well, you persuade him. So that night Jaffe got to the concert with, with punch, went backstage and, and Louis got him backstage and he had a big dinner catered back there and he had a photographer there that took about 50 pictures of Louis and punch together. And then he put $500 in his pocket and Louis said, you know, to square everything. And then he wouldn't see anybody from the jazz club. Said they were lined up at the door, you know, but he wouldn't see anybody from jazz.
